text: 🇲🇽⚖️ "For those who say there is no democracy in the country: it was a free vote." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 15, 2026 Most IMSS workers rejected the union's salary agreement in an open consultation. Sheinbaum credited the labor reform passed under López Obrador: workers can now vote on a deal negotiated by their union leadership. "If there had not been that labor reform, this would not have happened." IMSS director Zoé Robledo will open a new working table today and tomorrow for a better offer, with salary but also working conditions. "Nobody is obliged to do the impossible; what is possible, with the greatest benefit for IMSS workers."

🇲🇽✊ "When they tell us 'you look like Venezuela or Cuba': no. It is a model of our own, born from our history. It is called Mexican humanism, moral economy, and it is giving results." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 15, 2026 Asked what a future generation should understand about her government, Sheinbaum answered "shared prosperity," or "for the good of all, the poor first." She said López Obrador made great progress from 2018 to 2024, and according to ECLAC, Mexico accounts for 60% of the reduction in poverty in the region. The energy reforms now guarantee 54% public and 46% private electricity generation in law. And how does she want to be remembered? "As a good president, one who cared for and loved the people, and who did everything in her hands for the well-being of the people."

🇲🇽🇨🇳 <u>Tariffs Haven't Stopped It: Mexico's Deficit With China Hits $82.7 Billion</u>

Mexico's goods deficit with China grew 4.8% year on year from January to August 2026, to $82.721 billion, according to INEGI data reported by El Economista. That's despite the tariffs of 5% to 50% on 1,463 product lines that took effect on January 1.

Imports from China reached $92.655 billion (+8.7%). Mexican exports to China jumped 58.1%, to $9.934 billion, but that's barely a tenth of what comes in, and most of it is copper, lead and zinc concentrates.

At this pace, 2026 would be a third straight record for both imports from China and the deficit.

🇲🇽🎓 <u>First New UNAM Campus in Mexico City in Over 50 Years: Room for 20,000 Students</u>

At her second annual report, Mexico City Mayor Clara Brugada announced a new UNAM campus in the city's southeast, its first new campus in the capital in more than five decades. Nothing of this scale has been started since the five ENES units opened between 1973 and 1976.

"El gobierno de la ciudad va a construir este gran plantel para 20 mil estudiantes, por etapas, y la UNAM lo va a equipar y lo va a operar." (The city government will build this campus for 20,000 students in stages, and UNAM will equip and run it.)

There will also be three new public universities on the city's outskirts and five high schools in pueblos and barrios originarios, so that, in her words, "ningún joven tenga que alejarse de su comunidad para alcanzar sus sueños" (no young person has to leave their community to reach their dreams).

🇲🇽🏛️ <u>Senate Passes the Cadastral Law: One Code for Every Property in Mexico</u>

Mexico's Senate approved the General Law for the Strengthening and Harmonization of Cadastral and Property Registry Systems, 89 votes to 32, and sent it to the president for publication. Morena and its allies voted yes. PAN, PRI and MC voted no.

Under the law, every property in the country will get a single cadastral and registry ID code, procedures will be standardized nationwide, and municipalities will get two digital platforms, one for the cadastre and one for the Public Property Registry.

The opposition says it's a hidden property-tax hike and an attack on municipal powers. Morena rejected both claims.

🇲🇽⚖️ <u>Sheinbaum to the Army: Answer for Alicia de los Ríos</u>

Alicia de los Ríos Merino was a 25-year-old engineering student from Chihuahua and a member of the Liga Comunista 23 de Septiembre. She was disappeared on January 5, 1978, during the PRI's dirty war, and the Defense Ministry still hasn't handed over its files on her.

In August, an administrative court ruled that the military had failed to make its dirty-war archives public. On Thursday, President Sheinbaum said the Defense Ministry has to respond to that ruling, and that her government is working with the Comité Eureka on three fronts: the State recognizing forced disappearance as a practice ordered from the top, truth and justice, and finding the disappeared.

Her daughter, who carries the same name, is still looking for her.
banner: DIRTY WAR: ARMY MUST OPEN ITS FILES

🇲🇽🏠 <u>Housing Registrations Up 200%, Driven by Vivienda para el Bienestar</u>

New housing projects registered in Mexico jumped 200% in the first half of 2026 versus the first half of 2022, according to BBVA Research via El Economista, pushed mainly by the social-housing segment tied to Sheinbaum's Vivienda para el Bienestar.

By June the national housing registry counted 389,000 homes in production and unsold, up 84.6% in a year. The bottleneck: 154,000 of them (39.6%) show no progress or less than 20%. The program already has 667,000 homes under contract, 37% of its 1.8 million goal.

"It's not an easy task; a goal of 1.8 million homes is a lot... we should be a little patient," said Samuel Vázquez, BBVA Research's chief economist for Mexico.

🇲🇽✊ <u>282,000 IMSS Workers Vote by Secret Ballot, and Say No to 6.8%</u>

Mexico's Social Security (IMSS) workers voted on their own contract raise on October 14, in a secret-ballot consultation supervised by the Federal Labor Conciliation and Registration Center. About 282,000 took part, close to 60% of those eligible, at 670 polling stations.

The offer, 2.9% on base pay plus 3.9% in benefits, lost. "The results are clear. The majority of those who participated decided not to approve the salary proposal," said SNTSS union leader Rafael Olivos, who now goes back to the table with IMSS.

Before the 2019 labor reform, union bosses signed these deals behind closed doors.
banner: IMSS WORKERS VOTE NO ON 6.8% RAISE

🔥🇲🇽 <u>The PRI's Political Police Kept a File on El Universal's Owner</u>

Reports from the Federal Security Directorate (DFS), the PRI regime's political police, show it spied on Juan Francisco Ealy Ortiz, director of El Universal, in the mid-1980s.

The agents' verdict: he spent little time on journalism and a lot on "gestoría ante la administración pública", lobbying the government for his other businesses. The DFS filed El Universal as critical of the government but a "defender of business groups," and went through his correspondence too.

Ealy Ortiz still runs El Universal.
banner: DFS FILE: EL UNIVERSAL'S OWNER SPIED ON

🇲🇽⚖️ <u>Supreme Court: Five Votes Are Enough to Force a Congress to Do Its Job</u>

Mexico's Supreme Court ruled that a simple majority, five of nine justices, is now enough to declare that a state congress failed to legislate and order it to fix that. The old bar was six.

First case: Quintana Roo's legislature never set rules guaranteeing that people with disabilities can run for municipal office. Now it has to consult them and pass the law before the legal cutoff for changing election rules ahead of 2030.

Justice Loretta Ortiz Ahlf cast the deciding vote, 5–4.
banner: SUPREME COURT: 5 VOTES TO FORCE A LAW
